components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的名声很好,总是排长队。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de míngshēng hěn hǎo, zǒngshì pái chángduì.
example.english: This restaurant has a great reputation and there's always a long line.
example.fact: The Michelin Guide, now the world's most influential restaurant rating system, began in 1900 as a free booklet handed out by a French tire company to encourage more people to drive — and therefore wear out more tires. Its star ratings only became a serious culinary benchmark decades later.

meanings: variant of 發布|发布[fa1 bu4]

components.note: 发 is the simplified form of 發, which pictured a hand drawing back a bow to release an arrow — the sense of 'releasing' or 'sending out' extended to meanings like 'to issue' and 'to develop.'
巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'

example.hanzi: 公司明天将发布新产品。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī míngtiān jiāng fābù xīn chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The company will release a new product tomorrow.
example.fact: The first iPhone was announced in January 2007, but Apple had not yet finalized the software — engineers were still working out crashes and dropped calls in the weeks leading up to Steve Jobs's live demo, carefully routing his path across the stage to avoid the spots with the weakest signal.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) is close in sound to 英's reading yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
Person — describes a person's good qualities.
夋 (qūn) is related in sound to jùn but the two have drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他长得很英俊,吸引了很多人的目光。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn yīngjùn, xīyǐn le hěn duō rén de mùguāng.
example.english: He is very handsome and attracts a lot of attention.
example.fact: Facial symmetry is one of the most consistent cross-cultural predictors of how attractive a face is judged to be, because it can signal developmental stability and the absence of disease or injury during growth. Studies using digitally averaged, symmetrical composite faces find they are rated as more appealing than almost any individual face used to build them.

components.note: 工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) is close in sound to 室's reading shì

example.hanzi: 她在这个工作室里画了很多油画。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhège gōngzuòshì lǐ huà le hěn duō yóuhuà.
example.english: She has painted many oil paintings in this studio.
example.fact: Claude Monet's studio garden at Giverny, with its water lily pond and Japanese footbridge, was designed and planted by Monet himself specifically to serve as a living subject — he painted the pond in roughly 250 canvases over the last three decades of his life, watching it change with the light and seasons.

components.note: A drawing of a tree trunk with branches spreading up and roots below.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 工人用木头做了一张桌子。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén yòng mùtou zuò le yī zhāng zhuōzi.
example.english: The worker made a table out of wood.
example.fact: The tallest trees on Earth, coast redwoods, can grow taller than 115 meters and live for over 2,000 years, yet they have surprisingly shallow root systems — often only 3 to 4 meters deep. They survive storms by spreading their roots wide and intertwining them with neighboring trees for mutual support.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) is close in sound to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'

example.hanzi: 这次旅行的预算是五千元。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǔxíng de yùsuàn shì wǔqiān yuán.
example.english: The budget for this trip is five thousand yuan.
example.fact: NASA's original budget estimate for the Apollo program in 1961 was around $7 billion, but by the time of the first Moon landing in 1969 total spending had risen to roughly $25 billion — about $150 billion in today's dollars — driven by the accelerated timeline of the space race against the Soviet Union.

components.note: 田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) matches the sound of 然, which is also pronounced rán.

example.hanzi: 我猜他会迟到,果然他晚了半小时。
example.pinyin: Wǒ cāi tā huì chídào, guǒrán tā wǎn le bàn xiǎoshí.
example.english: I guessed he'd be late, and sure enough he was half an hour behind.
example.fact: Weather forecasters' predictions for tomorrow are correct roughly 80-90% of the time in most regions, but accuracy drops steeply beyond about a week because the atmosphere is a chaotic system — tiny, unmeasurable differences in starting conditions can snowball into completely different outcomes, a phenomenon known as the butterfly effect.

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows 锁 is typically a metal object.
⺌ (a form of 小) is distantly related in sound to suǒ, having drifted apart over time.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 手机屏幕已经锁定,需要输入密码。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī píngmù yǐjīng suǒdìng, xūyào shūrù mìmǎ.
example.english: The phone screen is locked and requires a password to unlock.
example.fact: Modern smartphone fingerprint sensors don't store an actual image of your fingerprint at all — they convert the ridge pattern into a mathematical template and keep it in an isolated secure enclave chip, so even if a phone's main storage is compromised, the fingerprint data itself typically can't be reconstructed from it.

components.note: 图 is the simplified form of 圖, which pictured a district's borders 啚 enclosed within a boundary 囗 — an old image of a map, giving 图 its meaning 'picture, chart, map.'
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 他在网上发了几张旅行的图片。
example.pinyin: Tā zài wǎngshàng fā le jǐ zhāng lǚxíng de túpiàn.
example.english: He posted a few pictures of his trip online.
example.fact: The first permanent photograph, taken by Joseph Nicéphore Niépce in 1826 or 1827, required an exposure time of roughly eight hours, capturing sunlight moving across a courtyard so that shadows appear on both sides of buildings in the same shot — a giveaway that the sun had crossed most of the sky during the exposure.

components.note: 自 here depicts a head (the character also independently means 'nose, self').
丷 depicts hair atop the head — 首 originally pictured a head with hair, giving its meaning 'head, chief, first.'
广 depicts a simple roofed building or shelter.
巾 (cloth) — together with a grass-like element above it, suggests a woven straw or cloth mat inside the shelter, giving 席 its meaning 'mat, seat.'

example.hanzi: 她是这家公司的首席设计师。
example.pinyin: Tā shì zhè jiā gōngsī de shǒuxí shèjìshī.
example.english: She is the company's chief designer.
example.fact: The title 'Chief Executive Officer' only became common in the United States in the 1960s and 70s; before that, companies more often used titles like 'President' or 'General Manager,' and the modern C-suite naming pattern (CFO, COO, CTO) spread largely because it gave a clear, comparable hierarchy for investors and boards.

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'

example.hanzi: 政府将在下周公布新的政策。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiāng zài xià zhōu gōngbù xīn de zhèngcè.
example.english: The government will announce a new policy next week.
example.fact: Ancient Rome's Twelve Tables of law, drafted around 450 BC, were literally posted in the Forum on bronze or wooden tablets so that ordinary citizens could see the laws for themselves — one of the earliest known examples of a government publicly codifying and displaying its legal rules rather than leaving them to the memory of elite judges.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 患 describes a burden weighing on the mind, worry or suffering.
串 (chuàn) is close in rhyme to huàn, though the initial consonant differs.
者 originally depicted a person stopping to speak, later becoming a general suffix meaning 'the one who...' or 'a person who does something,' as in 患者 ('sufferer') or 记者 ('reporter').

example.hanzi: 医院里的患者正在等待医生。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ de huànzhě zhèngzài děngdài yīshēng.
example.english: The patients in the hospital are waiting for the doctor.
example.fact: The placebo effect is strong enough that in clinical drug trials, patients given an inert sugar pill often report measurable improvement in symptoms like pain or nausea, simply from believing they received real medicine — which is why new drugs must beat a placebo, not just outperform doing nothing, to be approved.

meanings: the remaining years of one's life

components.note: 余 is the simplified form of 餘, which combined 食 (food/eating) with a phonetic element — food left over after a meal gave the character its meaning 'surplus, remaining, extra.'
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 他决定余生都住在这个小村子里。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng yúshēng dōu zhù zài zhège xiǎo cūnzi lǐ.
example.english: He decided to spend the rest of his life living in this small village.
example.fact: Jane Goodall began observing wild chimpanzees at Tanzania's Gombe Stream in 1960 and continued studying and advocating for them for the rest of her life, spanning over six decades — her early discovery that chimps use and make tools overturned the belief that tool use was a uniquely human trait.

components.note: A hand with a stick — represents striking or hitting.
高 (gāo) is related in sound to qiāo but the two have drifted apart over time.
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 有人在敲门,你能去开一下吗?
example.pinyin: Yǒurén zài qiāomén, nǐ néng qù kāi yīxià ma?
example.english: Someone is knocking on the door, can you go open it?
example.fact: Woodpeckers can strike a tree trunk up to 20 times per second, and their skulls have evolved a spongy layer of bone plus a tongue that wraps around the back of the skull to act as a cushioning strap — adaptations that keep the repeated impacts from causing brain injury.

components.note: 亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 我们打算在新年那天去看烟花。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn zài xīnnián nà tiān qù kàn yānhuā.
example.english: We plan to go watch fireworks on New Year's Day.
example.fact: January 1st was fixed as New Year's Day by the Romans in 46 BC when Julius Caesar introduced the Julian calendar, naming the month after Janus, the two-faced god who looked simultaneously into the past and the future — a fitting symbol for the turn of a year.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the weapon being drawn.
丨 depicts the taut drawstring being pulled back — giving 引 its meaning 'to pull, draw out, attract.'
发 is the simplified form of 發, which pictured a hand drawing back a bow to release an arrow — the sense of 'releasing' or 'sending out' extended to meanings like 'to issue' and 'to develop.'

example.hanzi: 这条新闻引发了社会的广泛讨论。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén yǐnfā le shèhuì de guǎngfàn tǎolùn.
example.english: This news triggered widespread discussion in society.
example.fact: The 2010 'flash crash' in US stock markets wiped out nearly a trillion dollars of value in about 36 minutes, triggered largely by high-frequency trading algorithms reacting to each other's rapid sell orders in a runaway feedback loop, before the market recovered most of its losses the same day.

components.note: 阝 (a mound, a place) — 阴 relates to the shaded side of a hill.
月 (moon) — the moon, associated with night and shade, gave 阴 its meaning 'shady, overcast'; compare 阳, which uses 日 (sun) for the opposite, sunny meaning.
彡 (fine lines) — suggests light and shadow, relating to 影's meaning 'shadow, image.'
景 (jǐng) is close in sound to 影's reading yǐng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.

example.hanzi: 那场事故给他留下了心理阴影。
example.pinyin: Nà chǎng shìgù gěi tā liúxià le xīnlǐ yīnyǐng.
example.english: That accident left a psychological shadow over him.
example.fact: A total solar eclipse's shadow, called the umbra, is typically only about 100-160 kilometers wide even though the Moon is 3,474 kilometers across, because the Moon must be almost exactly the same apparent size as the Sun in the sky — a coincidence that won't last forever, since the Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth.

components.note: 彡 (fine lines) — suggests light and shadow, relating to 影's meaning 'shadow, image.'
景 (jǐng) is close in sound to 影's reading yǐng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 这部影片在国际电影节上获得了大奖。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù yǐngpiàn zài guójì diànyǐngjié shàng huòdé le dàjiǎng.
example.english: This film won a major award at the international film festival.
example.fact: The Cannes Film Festival was originally planned to launch in September 1939 as a response to fascist influence over the Venice Film Festival, but it was cancelled after just one day when Germany invaded Poland, and the festival didn't actually begin until 1946.

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 他是下棋的高手,很少输。
example.pinyin: Tā shì xiàqí de gāoshǒu, hěn shǎo shū.
example.english: He's a chess expert and rarely loses.
example.fact: In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue became the first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion, Garry Kasparov, in a full match under tournament conditions — Kasparov later accused IBM of cheating, but analysis has generally attributed the loss to a buggy move by Deep Blue that Kasparov misread as a sign of superhuman insight, unsettling him for the rest of the match.

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — many early villages were built among or from trees and wood
寸 (cùn) is close in sound to 村's reading cūn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 这个村子里只有几十户人家。
example.pinyin: Zhège cūnzi lǐ zhǐyǒu jǐshí hù rénjiā.
example.english: There are only a few dozen households in this village.
example.fact: Hallstatt, a small Austrian village of fewer than 800 residents built on the edge of an alpine lake, has become so popular with tourists partly because a nearly identical full-scale replica was built in Boluo, China in 2012 — sparking a wave of visitors who wanted to see the real version.

components.note: 氵 (water) — growth and nourishment are tied to water.
兹 (zī) matches the sound of 滋 exactly.
口 (mouth) — 味 relates to taste, sensed in the mouth.
未 (wèi) matches the sound of 味 exactly.

example.hanzi: 这道菜的滋味非常特别。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de zīwèi fēicháng tèbié.
example.english: The flavor of this dish is very unique.
example.fact: Umami, the savory fifth basic taste alongside sweet, sour, salty, and bitter, was identified in 1908 by Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda, who traced it to glutamate in kombu seaweed broth — but it wasn't formally recognized by Western food science until dedicated umami taste receptors were confirmed on the tongue in the early 2000s.

components.note: 手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 导演用了一种独特的手法来讲这个故事。
example.pinyin: Dǎoyǎn yòng le yī zhǒng dútè de shǒufǎ lái jiǎng zhège gùshì.
example.english: The director used a unique technique to tell this story.
example.fact: Alfred Hitchcock pioneered a camera technique now called the 'dolly zoom,' where the camera physically moves backward while the lens zooms in at the same time, distorting perspective to create a disorienting, vertigo-like sensation — he used it in the 1958 film Vertigo to visualize the protagonist's fear of heights.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — 右 originally pictured a hand, later combined with 口 (mouth), possibly from the idea of the hand one uses to eat or gesture with, coming to mean 'right side.'
口 (mouth) — added below the hand element to distinguish 右 ('right') from 左 ('left'), which pairs the hand shape with a tool instead.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 他用右手写字。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng yòushǒu xiězì.
example.english: He writes with his right hand.
example.fact: About 90% of people are right-handed, a ratio that has stayed remarkably stable across cultures and centuries, and researchers have traced evidence of this same left-brain dominance for tool use back to Homo habilis stone tools roughly 1.8 million years old, suggesting handedness has deep evolutionary roots tied to brain lateralization.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) hints at the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
氵 (water) — 洋 refers to the vast ocean
羊 (yáng) matches the sound of 洋's reading yáng exactly

example.hanzi: 太平洋是世界上最大的海洋。
example.pinyin: Tàipíngyáng shì shìjiè shàng zuìdà de hǎiyáng.
example.english: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
example.fact: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square kilometers — larger than the combined landmass of every continent on Earth — and its deepest point, the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep, plunges nearly 11,000 meters, deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with over a kilometer of ocean left above its peak.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 霍 pictures a sudden downpour.
隹 (a short-tailed bird) — birds startled and scattered by a sudden storm of rain 雨 gave 霍 its meaning 'suddenly, quickly.'
十 (ten, suggesting abundance) — relates to 华's meaning 'flowery, splendid,' an abundance of blossoms.
化 (huà) hints at the sound — 华 is pronounced huá, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.

example.hanzi: 霍华德是我们公司新来的经理。
example.pinyin: Huòhuádé shì wǒmen gōngsī xīnlái de jīnglǐ.
example.english: Howard is the new manager who just joined our company.
example.fact: Howard Carter, the British archaeologist whose name shares its Chinese transliteration pattern with names like Howard, spent nearly a decade searching the Valley of the Kings before discovering the almost fully intact tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922 — one of the most significant archaeological finds of the 20th century.

components.note: 冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 他的爱好是收集老照片。
example.pinyin: Tā de àihào shì shōují lǎo zhàopiàn.
example.english: His hobby is collecting old photographs.
example.fact: Philately, the hobby of stamp collecting, exploded in popularity within a few years of the first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, being issued by Britain in 1840 — one rare example, the 1856 British Guiana One-Cent Magenta, later sold at auction for over $9 million, making it the most valuable stamp in the world.

components.note: 乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'
见 (to see) — the act of looking.
又 (again, or a hand) — looking closely or repeatedly, giving 观 its meaning 'to observe, view.'

example.hanzi: 即使遇到困难,她也一直很乐观。
example.pinyin: Jíshǐ yùdào kùnnán, tā yě yīzhí hěn lèguān.
example.english: Even when facing difficulties, she always stays optimistic.
example.fact: The Nun Study, a long-running research project on a convent of Catholic nuns, found that sisters who wrote more positive, optimistic language in autobiographical essays as young adults in the 1930s and 40s lived on average about 10 years longer than those with less positive language, one of the strongest links found between outlook and longevity.

components.note: 刂 (a knife) — 创 relates to cutting or wounding, extended to mean 'to start, to create,' as a fresh cut marks a new beginning
仓 (cāng) has a loose sound connection to 创's reading chuàng
亻 (person) — 伤 relates to physical harm done to a person's body.
𠂉 (a variant form related to 刀, a blade) — a person cut or struck, giving 伤 its meaning 'wound, injury; to hurt.'

example.hanzi: 士兵在战场上留下了严重的创伤。
example.pinyin: Shìbīng zài zhànchǎng shàng liúxià le yánzhòng de chuāngshāng.
example.english: The soldier suffered a serious wound on the battlefield.
example.fact: During World War I, the introduction of steel helmets is estimated to have reduced fatal head wounds among soldiers by as much as 75%, prompting armies across Europe to rapidly replace cloth and leather caps — a shift driven directly by battlefield medical data on the most common causes of death.

components.note: 至 depicts an arrow reaching the ground after landing — arriving at a destination gave 至 its meaning 'to arrive' or 'until.'
亼 — traditionally linked to an image of gathering or covering; its original pictorial sense has become obscure, but the character came to mean 'now, the present.'

example.hanzi: 这个问题至今没有得到解决。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí zhìjīn méiyǒu dédào jiějué.
example.english: This problem still hasn't been resolved to this day.
example.fact: The Voynich Manuscript, a roughly 240-page handwritten book filled with an unknown script and bizarre illustrations of plants and astrological symbols, has resisted every attempt at decipherment since it resurfaced in 1912 — carbon dating places the vellum to the early 1400s, but no one has confirmed to this day whether it encodes a real language, a cipher, or an elaborate hoax.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) is close in sound to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'

example.hanzi: 运动员正在预备明天的比赛。
example.pinyin: Yùndòngyuán zhèngzài yùbèi míngtiān de bǐsài.
example.english: The athletes are preparing for tomorrow's competition.
example.fact: Olympic gymnasts often train for six to eight hours a day, six days a week, for years before a single competition, and elite programs like those in Romania and China have historically started identifying and training prospective gymnasts as young as five or six years old, decades before an athlete might reach the Olympic stage.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 损 relates to damage or loss caused by an action.
员 (yuán) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading sǔn has diverged.
亻 (person) — 伤 relates to physical harm done to a person's body.
𠂉 (a variant form related to 刀, a blade) — a person cut or struck, giving 伤 its meaning 'wound, injury; to hurt.'

example.hanzi: 长时间用眼会损伤视力。
example.pinyin: Cháng shíjiān yòngyǎn huì sǔnshāng shìlì.
example.english: Using your eyes for a long time can damage your eyesight.
example.fact: Prolonged exposure to loud noise above about 85 decibels — roughly the volume of heavy city traffic — can permanently damage the tiny hair cells in the inner ear that convert sound vibrations into nerve signals, and unlike many other cells in the human body, these hair cells do not regenerate once destroyed.

components.note: 亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
廾 depicts two hands.
敝 shows something worn out or broken — together suggesting hands causing damage, which is how 弊 came to mean 'harm, malpractice.'

example.hanzi: 考试作弊会受到严重的处罚。
example.pinyin: Kǎoshì zuòbì huì shòudào yánzhòng de chǔfá.
example.english: Cheating on an exam will result in serious punishment.
example.fact: In imperial China's civil service examinations, which could last up to three days and determined access to government office, some candidates smuggled in cheat sheets sewn into the lining of their clothing — surviving examples show thousands of tiny handwritten characters covering entire silk undergarments, some now preserved in museums.

components.note: 氵 (water/stream) — the water being crossed.
步 (to step, walk) — feet moving through it, together giving 涉 its meaning 'to wade across' and, more broadly, 'to be involved in.'
及 pictures a hand 又 reaching out to catch up with a person ahead — the source of its meaning 'to reach, catch up to; and, together with.'

example.hanzi: 这个案子涉及多个国家的公司。
example.pinyin: Zhège ànzi shèjí duō gè guójiā de gōngsī.
example.english: This case involves companies from multiple countries.
example.fact: The 2015 Volkswagen emissions scandal involved software installed in roughly 11 million diesel vehicles worldwide that could detect when a car was undergoing an emissions test and temporarily reduce pollution output, only to revert to much higher, illegal emission levels during ordinary driving.

components.note: 彳 (a step/road) — 征 relates to a long journey or military campaign
正 (zhèng) is close in sound to 征's reading zhēng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'

example.hanzi: 登山者最终征服了这座高峰。
example.pinyin: Dēngshānzhě zuìzhōng zhēngfú le zhè zuò gāofēng.
example.english: The climber finally conquered this high peak.
example.fact: Mount Everest was first confirmed climbed to its summit in 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, but the mountain still claims lives nearly every climbing season — the 'death zone' above 8,000 meters has so little oxygen that human bodies begin dying cell by cell even while resting, which is why speed and weather timing are critical to survival.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
尸, here a variant of 厂, depicts a roof or shelter.
至 depicts arriving or coming to rest — settling under a roof gave 屋 its meaning 'house, room.'

example.hanzi: 他们在山上盖了一间小屋。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài shānshàng gài le yī jiān xiǎowū.
example.english: They built a small cabin on the mountain.
example.fact: Henry David Thoreau's famous cabin at Walden Pond, the setting for his 1854 book Walden, measured only about 10 by 15 feet — roughly the size of a modern one-car garage — and he built most of it himself for around $28, a deliberate experiment in simple living close to nature.

components.note: 罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.
木 (tree) — 杰 is the simplified form of 傑, which combined a person-related element with a phonetic component; today it's used to mean 'outstanding, heroic' and is common in given names.
灬 here functions as a simplified phonetic/structural element rather than its usual meaning 'fire,' completing 杰's shape.

example.hanzi: 罗杰是我大学时最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Luójié shì wǒ dàxué shí zuìhǎo de péngyǒu.
example.english: Roger was my best friend during college.
example.fact: Roger Bannister became the first person to run a mile in under four minutes in 1954, clocking 3:59.4 — a barrier many physiologists at the time believed was beyond human capability — and remarkably, another runner broke his new record just 46 days later, showing how much of the limit had been psychological.

components.note: Hand — moving things is done by hand.
般 (bān) matches the character's reading bān exactly.
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) is close in sound to 进's reading jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.

example.hanzi: 他们下个月要搬进新房子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen xià gè yuè yào bānjìn xīn fángzi.
example.english: They are moving into a new house next month.
example.fact: The Biosphere 2 project in Arizona sealed eight scientists inside a giant glass and steel enclosure for two years starting in 1991, growing their own food and recycling their own air and water, in an experiment meant to test whether humans could live self-sufficiently — a scaled-up rehearsal for one day moving into a habitat on Mars.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) matches the sound of 认's reading rèn closely.
罒 (a net) — the law closing in around wrongdoing
非 (wrong) — the wrongdoing itself, caught in the net

example.hanzi: 被告最终在法庭上认罪了。
example.pinyin: Bèigào zuìzhōng zài fǎtíng shàng rènzuì le.
example.english: The defendant finally pleaded guilty in court.
example.fact: Plea bargaining, where a defendant pleads guilty in exchange for a reduced sentence, resolves roughly 90-95% of criminal cases in the United States without ever going to trial, a proportion so high that some legal scholars argue the modern American justice system functions primarily as a system of negotiated pleas rather than trials by jury.

components.note: 又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'
羊 (sheep) — food offered generously to another person
口 (mouth) — kind words spoken alongside the gift

example.hanzi: 当地居民对游客都很友善。
example.pinyin: Dāngdì jūmín duì yóukè dōu hěn yǒushàn.
example.english: The local residents are all very friendly to tourists.
example.fact: Bonobos, close genetic relatives of chimpanzees, are notably less aggressive toward strangers and more prone to sharing food with unfamiliar individuals than chimps are, a difference researchers link partly to bonobo societies being led by females and to lower competition for food in their central African habitat.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 称 originally involved weighing grain on a scale.
尔 (ěr) contributes to the character's structure and, in its full traditional form 稱, its sound; 称 came to mean 'to weigh; to call, name.'
A stylized foot (related to 止, 'to stop/foot') — originally meant 'to go,' later grammaticalized into a literary possessive/linking particle, similar to 的.
为 is the simplified form of 為, which originally pictured a hand 爪 leading an elephant 象 — training an elephant to work gave the character its broad meaning 'to do, to act as, to be.'

example.hanzi: 人们称之为世界第八大奇迹。
example.pinyin: Rénmen chēngzhīwéi shìjiè dì bā dà qíjì.
example.english: People call it the eighth wonder of the world.
example.fact: The original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World were first listed by Greek writers around the 2nd century BC, but only one of them, the Great Pyramid of Giza, still survives today — the other six, including the Hanging Gardens of Babylon and the Colossus of Rhodes, were destroyed by earthquakes, fire, or war over the centuries.

components.note: 冎 pictures a joint of bone.
⺼ (flesh) sits below, together giving 骨 its meaning 'bone.'
扌 (hand) does the action.
斤 (axe) — chopping and snapping something in two gives 折 its meaning 'to break, to bend.'

example.hanzi: 他滑雪时不小心骨折了。
example.pinyin: Tā huáxuě shí bùxiǎoxīn gǔzhé le.
example.english: He accidentally broke a bone while skiing.
example.fact: The human body has 206 bones in adulthood but starts life with about 270 to 300 at birth, because many bones — like the skull plates and parts of the spine — begin as separate pieces of cartilage or bone that fuse together as a child grows, which is also why fractures in children often heal faster than in adults.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
亻 (person) — 仇 describes a person one holds a grudge against, 'an enemy.'
九 (jiǔ) is only distantly related in sound to chóu — the connection has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他花了十年时间才为父亲报仇。
example.pinyin: Tā huā le shí nián shíjiān cái wèi fùqīn bàochóu.
example.english: It took him ten years to finally avenge his father.
example.fact: The Count of Monte Cristo, Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel of imprisonment and elaborate revenge, was partly inspired by a real police file Dumas encountered about François Picaud, a Frenchman falsely imprisoned by jealous friends who spent years methodically ruining each of their lives after his release.

components.note: 虫 (insect/small creature) — in old classification schemes, bats were grouped with insects and other small creatures rather than mammals.
扁 (biǎn) is close in sound to 蝙's reading biān, differing only in tone.
虫 (insect) — the insect radical, originally depicting a snake-like shape, marking the character as related to insects or small creatures.
畐 (fú) matches the sound of 蝠's reading exactly; 畐 is the shared root behind other fú characters like 副 and 富.

example.hanzi: 蝙蝠在夜里靠回声定位捕食。
example.pinyin: Biānfú zài yèlǐ kào huíshēng dìngwèi bǔshí.
example.english: Bats hunt at night using echolocation.
example.fact: Bats are the only mammals capable of true, sustained flight, and many species navigate and hunt in complete darkness using echolocation — emitting high-frequency calls, some above 100 kHz, and interpreting the returning echoes with enough precision to detect an insect the width of a human hair in midair.

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 全家人一起去海边度假。
example.pinyin: Quánjiā rén yīqǐ qù hǎibiān dùjià.
example.english: The whole family went to the seaside for vacation together.
example.fact: China's Spring Festival travel period, when hundreds of millions of people journey home to reunite with family for the Lunar New Year, is the largest annual human migration on Earth — in recent years, total trips during the roughly 40-day travel window have exceeded 2 billion, more than the population of every country except China and India combined.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 春 relates to spring's longer, sunnier days.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 春天到了,花都开了。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān dào le, huā dōu kāi le.
example.english: Spring has arrived, and all the flowers are blooming.
example.fact: Japan's cherry blossom season, celebrated in the tradition of hanami, typically lasts only about one to two weeks per location, and meteorologists track the 'blossom front' as it moves northward across the country each spring — the Japan Meteorological Agency has published official forecasts for peak bloom dates since 1951.

components.note: 氵 (water) — muddiness and turbidity describe a state of water.
军 (jūn) is distantly related in sound to hún, having drifted apart over time.
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 跑完马拉松后他浑身都疼。
example.pinyin: Pǎowán mǎlāsōng hòu tā húnshēn dōu téng.
example.english: After finishing the marathon, his whole body ached.
example.fact: The soreness felt all over the body a day or two after intense exercise, known as delayed onset muscle soreness, is caused by microscopic tears in muscle fibers rather than lactic acid buildup, a myth that persisted for decades — lactic acid actually clears from the muscles within about an hour of exercise ending.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) hints at the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
扌 (hand) — 搅 describes stirring something with the hands.
觉 (jiào) is close in sound to jiǎo, the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 抱歉打搅你了,我能问个问题吗?
example.pinyin: Bàoqiàn dǎjiǎo nǐ le, wǒ néng wèn gè wèntí ma?
example.english: Sorry to disturb you, may I ask a question?
example.fact: The 'Do Not Disturb' sign hung on hotel doorknobs is believed to date back to the early 20th century as hotels standardized guest privacy signals, and by the mid-1900s it had become such a universal fixture that some hotel chains began printing branded, novelty, or humorous versions as a form of guest amenity.

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 近's meaning 'near, close,' a short distance to walk.
斤 (jīn) hints at the sound — 近 is pronounced jìn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子从小就跟爷爷很亲近。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi cóngxiǎo jiù gēn yéye hěn qīnjìn.
example.english: This child has been close to his grandfather since childhood.
example.fact: Studies of attachment in early childhood, beginning with British psychologist John Bowlby's work in the 1950s, found that a secure, closely bonded relationship with at least one consistent caregiver in the first years of life is one of the strongest predictors of emotional resilience and healthy relationships later in adulthood.

components.note: 爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'
讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.

example.hanzi: 两位专家就这个问题展开了激烈的争论。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi zhuānjiā jiù zhège wèntí zhǎnkāi le jīliè de zhēnglùn.
example.english: The two experts engaged in a fierce debate over this issue.
example.fact: The Great Debate of 1920 was a formal astronomical dispute between Harlow Shapley and Heber Curtis over whether the Andromeda Nebula was part of the Milky Way or a separate, distant galaxy — the question wasn't settled until 1923, when Edwin Hubble measured Cepheid variable stars in Andromeda and proved it lay far outside our own galaxy.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) hints at the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 参加会议的人数比预期多。
example.pinyin: Cānjiā huìyì de rénshù bǐ yùqī duō.
example.english: The number of people attending the meeting was more than expected.
example.fact: Woodstock, the 1969 music festival planned for an audience of about 50,000, ended up drawing an estimated 400,000 attendees — far exceeding food, water, and sanitation capacity — and the surrounding roads became so gridlocked that many performers had to be flown in by helicopter to reach the stage on time.
